news.title: USA exits U-20 World Cup on penalties as tournament’s timing draws criticism
news.lede: Brazil advances to quarter-finals in Poland. Americans have not won tournament since 2012. US youth teams have struggled in recent showings. The United States were eliminated from the U-20 Women’s World Cup in the last 16 on Wednesday, falling to Brazil on penalties after playing to a 1-1 draw after extra-time.

news.title: Thomas Tuchel explains how Argentina’s ‘f*** it football’ dismantled England in World Cup failure
news.lede: Thomas Tuchel has opened up on England’s World Cup semi-final capitulation and how Argentina’s “f***-it football” left his team “waiting for death”. England achieved their best World Cup finish since 1966 this summer, taking home bronze after defeating France 6-4 in a thrilling third-place play-off in Miami. However, their campaign was defined by gut-wrenching semi-final failure against Argentina, which saw England surrender a lead to the defending champions before losing in stoppage time. The tide of the match seemed to shift in Argentina’s favour after Tuchel went heavily defensive, going to a back-five by bringing on Ezri Konsa with 20 minutes to play, before having the team sit back.

news.title: Al Mouj Muscat supports Oman U15 for World Cup
news.lede: ​MUSCAT: Al Mouj Muscat, the Sultanate of Oman’s premier destination for major sporting and lifestyle events, has announced its sponsorship of the Oman U15 national football team as they prepare to represent Oman at the upcoming U15 World Cup. The partnership with the Oman Football Association (OFA) reflects a shared commitment to investing in young Omani talent and creating opportunities that contribute to the long-term development of national sport. The 14-player national squad will represent Oman at the inaugural Fifa U15 World Cup 2026 in Azerbaijan, beginning on October 22. The milestone represents a significant step forward for Omani youth football, giving some of the country’s most promising young players the opportunity to test themselves internationally and gain valuable experience at a formative stage in their development.

news.title: Spain strike and tie down 'the best coach in the world' for the 2030 World Cup
news.lede: Luis de la Fuente has extended his contract with the Spanish Football Federation until the 2030 World Cup, federation president Rafael Louzan announced to Diario AS on Wednesday.De la Fuente has been Spain coach for the past three years. He replaced Luis Enrique in 2023 after the World Cup in Qatar.That appointment proved a masterstroke. In 2024, De la Fuente led Spain to the European Championship in Germany, beating England in the final.Two years later, Spain also won the World Cup in North America under his leadership. They beat Argentina 1-0 in the final.Previously in charge of, among others, Athletic Club and Alavés, the former manager was still under contract with the federation until mid-2028, but will now sign until mid-2030.

news.title: Veo Highlights the Power of Connection at the Special Olympics Unified Football World Cup
news.lede: Veo recently featured a story showcasing how access to live-streamed matches helped supporters around the world stay connected to the Special Olympics Unified Football World Cup, held in Paris from 6 to 11 July. The article, "They Are Footballers", highlights how the partnership between Special Olympics and Veo made it possible for families, friends, and fans around the world to follow the tournament through live streaming and match recordings. By expanding access to the competition, the collaboration helped ensure that athletes' achievements could be celebrated far beyond the stadium.
